pr_title: Fix the ranking rule by temporarily disabling an assert in the bucket sort algorithm
pr_body:
This PR temporarily disables an assertion, making the search crash. [I created a tracking issue](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/issues/4012) to find a better way to fix this.

It no longer reverts a20e4d447ce3022443d25223d34d1a7a8e98e31f, which seemed to generate unreachable graphs and make the bucket sort ranking algorithm panic because of entering an unreachable state. We discussed that below in the comments.

Temporary fixes #4002, fixes #4006, and fixes #3995.

---

It took me approximately 2 days to find the first bad commit just because I'm bad in `git bisect` x `bash`, i.e. [I misused `%1` with `$!` to kill the most recently backgrounded job](https://unix.stackexchange.com/a/340084/212574)...

<details>
  <summary>Here is the script I used to find the invalid commit</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -x

# remove the data
rm -rf data.ms

# build meilisearch
cargo build --release
# ignore this commit if it doesn't compile
if [[ $? != 0 ]]; then
    exit 125
fi

# index the dump and start from it
./target/release/meilisearch \
--http-addr 'localhost:7705' \
--import-dump $HOME/Downloads/modified-20230822-083016113.dump &

# wait 10 sec while it indexes the docs
sleep 5

# check if the server crashes on requests
echo '{
    "q": "rtx 305",
    "attributesToHighlight": [
        "*"
    ],
    "highlightPreTag": "<ais-highlight-0000000000>",
    "highlightPostTag": "</ais-highlight-0000000000>",
    "limit": 21,
    "offset": 0
}' | xh 'localhost:7705/indexes/arvutitark_local_orderables/search'

last_exit_code=$?

# Now kill Meilisearch
kill $!

# Clean the potential Cargo.lock
git checkout .

exit $last_exit_code
```
</details>
pr_comments:
Hello @Kerollmops :wave:

thanks for spending time on fixing this issue :heart:

Unfortunately, this PR reverts a relevancy fix of v1.3, so I'd rather we don't merge it.
Could we consider temporarily disabling the firing assert instead, if that doesn't cause wrong results?

<details>
<summary>
Motivation for the relevancy change
</summary>

Let's consider the query: `Batman the dark knight returns` and the documents:

```
{ "id": 0, "title": "Batman the dark knight returns" }
{ "id": 1, "title": "Dark the Batman knight returns" }
{ "id": 2, "title": "Batman returns: a retrospective", "description" : "The Dark knight is analyzed in this new Batman documentary" }
```
Before v1.3, the `position` ranking rule would put document with id 2 first, then documents 0 and 1 would be a tie.

After v1.3, the order is strictly: Document 0, Document 1, Document 2, which we feel is more natural

That's because to compute the score before v1.3, we would take the distance of each word in an attribute to position 0, so the total distance would be: `0+1+2+3+4=10` for id 0, `2+1+0+3+4=10` for id 1, and `0+0+1+2+1=4` for id 2.

After v1.3, since we take the distance to the position in the query, the total distance become `0+0+0+0+0=0` for id 0, `2+0+2+0+0=4` for id 1, `0+1+1+1+3=6` for id 2.

While this order was not very visible before v1.3, because of the new ranking score details the behavior becomes much more apparent: document 0 used to have a non-perfect score for position, which we felt was not intuitive at all.

Besides, if we allow separating attributes and position in future Meilisearch versions, the "distance to 0" implementation will lead to strange order of results.

Internal threads about that change:

- [Discussion of the change on the squad channel](https://meilisearch.slack.com/archives/C05A9SRPMFB/p1686640758803419)
- [Discussion of the change on the relevancy issues channel](https://meilisearch.slack.com/archives/C04QK4M2KMY/p1686640788657429)
- [Explanation of the change to for the changelog/release article](https://meilisearch.slack.com/archives/CD7AJLL01/p1688572266026429)

</details>

Thank you @dureuill 😊

I changed the PR content to disable the panicking assert temporarily and am waiting for you to come back or anyone on the team to see what we can do about this. But more importantly, we ensure we test it correctly to avoid releasing such issues in the wild.

Thanks kero,

I discussed this with lo back in the day but unfortunately we couldn't come up with a surefire way to lift this runtime panic to a compile error.

We didn't explore covering with tests, but I'm suspecting the input space is too large for this to be practically feasible.

I'll give it more thought when I'm back and I'll definitely investigate the behavior unless y'all already found the cause by then

Do the search results still make sense after removing the panic?

> I'll give it more thought when I'm back, and I'll investigate the behavior unless y'all already found the cause by then.

Thank you very much, Louis 😊

> Do the search results still make sense after removing the panic?

The results seem correct, but I only have one dataset and two or three queries. It is much better than crashing for now. But I also fear that some results are not shown anymore.
